native.text: Locking excludes `{facts.generated_cache_directory}` from the native build context. Also commit the updated ignore file.
The native lock records exact revisions; its companion records artifact hashes, original metadata, and resolution configuration.
OCI manifest, configuration, and layer identities retain their native SHA-256 digests. The lock adds platform selections and input fingerprints.

locked.text:
Run `{commands.lock}` after changing dependency declarations. Relocking retains existing pins.

Run `{commands.update}` to update dependencies, then `{commands.prefetch}`.
Update one selected dependency with `{commands.named-update} {facts.named_update_example}`. Other selected pins are retained.

fresh.text:
Run `{commands.lock}` after changing dependency declarations. Relocking resolves dependencies again; it does not retain existing pins.

Run `{commands.prefetch}` before building.
Update one selected dependency with `{commands.named-update} {facts.named_update_example}`. Other selected pins are retained.

wrapper.text: The shell supplies a wrapper for the native build tool. Without an applicable lock, it warns and runs the ordinary native tool. A stale or invalid lock fails with a repair command.
The supplied wrapper is required for native builds.
The integration handles {facts.supported_native_commands}; other native commands run normally.

Alternatively, activate the native plugin in the build. Resolve `{facts.native_plugin_coordinate}` from the [native plugin repository]({facts.native_plugin_repository}). Keep bootstrap dependencies separate from application dependencies.
Native Maven bootstrap resolution is impure; use the wrapper for pure plugin resolution.

scoped.text:
Run `{commands.prefetch}` to prepare the locked dependencies. This does not guarantee that the entire build can run offline.

Outside this lock: {facts.offline_limits}.
Prefetch retains {facts.prefetch_components} through garbage-collector roots beside the selected lockfile.

command.text: Configure your existing editor's Language Server Protocol (LSP) client to launch `{commands.editor}` from the development shell. This puts its language tooling in the same environment as the native build.
Diagnostics and definition lookup work offline after prefetch.
The language server can retrieve source code for locked dependencies.
The launcher prepares Eclipse project metadata with immutable dependency and source JAR paths.

builder.text:
Apply `overlays.default` and call `{facts.nix_builder}`.

The result exposes: {facts.build_outputs}.
The project builds in the Nix sandbox.
The builder runs {facts.build_engine} inside a networkless software VM.

platforms.text: The default CLI transport supports anonymous access. Builder fetcher overrides can integrate corporate transport.
